notes.title: Enforce input contracts before state can become invalid
notes.core: State the legitimate input domain explicitly. Reject invalid parameters at the boundary, especially when an argument is retained for deferred use, without adding arbitrary restrictions or expensive redundant pre-scans.
rules: Use Objects.requireNonNull for required references and document the externally observable null contract.
Choose a documented invalid-argument exception that matches the abstraction; distinguish malformed ranges, indexes, and null references.
Validate constructor inputs and deferred callbacks before changing state or publishing objects.
Use Objects.checkIndex/checkFromToIndex/checkFromIndexSize for their applicable half-open and length-based integer ranges; do not mistake them for arbitrary inclusive-range validators.
Assertions in internal helpers document programmer invariants but are disabled by default; never substitute them for public input validation.
Avoid duplicate expensive work when the computation reliably and promptly validates with the specified exception and cannot compromise state.
nuance: Validate offset and size together using overflow-safe arithmetic rather than offset + size when int overflow can hide a bad range.
Exception translation is suitable if a delegated operation rejects an invalid parameter using an exception inconsistent with the published contract.
Fail-fast validation is distinct from trying to prevalidate every possible I/O or concurrency outcome.
A non-null value may still violate a domain invariant such as negative amount, unknown account or invalid currency code.
requireNonNullElse and requireNonNullElseGet (available in Java 21) are fallback policies, not substitutions when null should be rejected.
notes.misconception: Because internal assertion checks passed locally, they will protect an exported API when assertions are disabled in production.
notes.production_context: An installment-plan constructor validates amount and currency before making an immutable rule object; the range-query endpoint rejects impossible indices without changing stored state.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 retains Objects.requireNonNull and Java 9-introduced range checking APIs; no reliance on enabled assertions or unsupported inclusive-end semantics.

notes.title: Make method signatures hard to misuse and easy to compose
notes.core: An API signature is an error-prevention mechanism: keep names consistent, keep parameter groups short and meaningful, and expose the weakest useful types rather than one concrete implementation.
rules: Use recognizable verbs with consistent package conventions and keep each convenience method justified by real usage.
Avoid long lists of same-typed parameters that can be silently transposed; represent a cohesive concept as a named immutable value.
Use smaller orthogonal operations when composition is clearer than one gigantic method.
For many optional inputs, consider a request object or staged builder with a single validated execution boundary.
Accept Map/List or other suitable interfaces instead of forcing HashMap/ArrayList at the signature.
Prefer a small enum over an ambiguous boolean switch unless the method name itself makes the boolean unambiguous.
nuance: The suggested small parameter count is a design heuristic, not a compiler-enforced limit.
A record groups parameters concisely in Java 21, but the compact constructor still needs invariants and public field-name compatibility thought.
A builder can create invalid intermediate states; validate before execution and avoid leaking partial operations.
Excess convenience overloads increase API surface, overload ambiguity and compatibility burden.
Java 21 SequencedCollection may help order-aware contracts but should not be used if ordinary Collection expresses the requirement.
notes.misconception: A method with many primitive or String parameters is safe because each call compiles and the IDE shows the argument labels.
notes.production_context: A refund request uses an immutable MoneyAmount plus a RefundMode enum; a reconciliation report accepts Map rather than requiring a specific implementation.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 records and sealed types offer concise parameters and modes beyond the book-era API toolkit, without changing the core advice on cohesion and interface types.

notes.title: Avoid overload surprises: static signatures versus dynamic overrides
notes.core: Method overload selection uses compile-time argument types, whereas instance overriding dispatches on runtime receiver type. Design public overloads so these distinct rules never create surprising domain behavior.
rules: Do not expect overload selection to perform runtime subclass classification; use one polymorphic operation or an explicit type test when required.
Prefer different method names to same-arity overloads whose argument sets overlap.
Treat overloads involving primitives, boxed wrappers and generic collections as possible behavioral traps.
Avoid overloads with different functional-interface targets in the same position, particularly with implicit lambdas or method references.
When compatibility forces overlapping overloads, delegate toward one canonical implementation and preserve equivalent behavior on common inputs.
A Java constructor cannot be overridden; use descriptive static factories if multiple construction routes are confusing.
nuance: A cast or explicit target type can change overload selection without changing the runtime object.
A null literal can be ambiguous between unrelated reference overloads; named methods avoid the trap.
List.remove(int) and List.remove(Object) differ by index and value; a boxed Integer argument matters.
Interface default methods and static method overloads still obey their distinct resolution rules; test the actual selected contract.
Pattern matching for instanceof in Java 21 can simplify explicit type dispatch but is not magic runtime overload selection.
notes.misconception: The most specific runtime subtype determines which overloaded method is invoked, just like overriding.
notes.production_context: An event router originally exposes overloaded register for incompatible handler interfaces; the corrected router names subscriptions by contract and dispatches event subtypes through polymorphism.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 pattern matching and lambdas add expressive code but overload resolution remains statically driven; current javac warnings and ambiguous-target checks still matter.

notes.title: Use varargs only when variable arity is the contract
notes.core: A varargs parameter is an array-based call convenience, not an assurance of non-empty input or zero allocation. Make required arguments regular parameters and use specialized fast paths only when measurement warrants them.
rules: Design a method requiring one input as first plus rest... to reject zero-argument calls at compile time.
Document whether zero values and a null supplied array have meaning; varargs calls can pass a null array explicitly.
Beware of argument-array creation and possible allocations when calling variable-arity APIs on hot paths.
Do not introduce a cluster of fixed-arity overloads based on hypothetical performance; measure representative workload first.
Handle generic varargs with heap-pollution warnings carefully and apply @SafeVarargs only when the implementation is actually safe.
Avoid unsafe writes to arrays that represent parameterized types and avoid exposing the mutable varargs array.
nuance: Fixed-arity overload dispatch may outrank a varargs match and can change behavior unexpectedly.
Calls passing an array directly can avoid an extra packed-varargs array, depending on overload and compilation path; do not promise an allocation count.
Java 21 List.of allows zero or many inputs but rejects null elements; that behavior is separate from varargs arity.
An explicit first element ensures at least one argument statically, but the first reference might still be null and require validation.
Static factory and constructor APIs often benefit from named collection alternatives if varargs makes validation ambiguous.
notes.misconception: Using T... automatically ensures at least one value and costs the same as ordinary fixed parameters.
notes.production_context: A reconciliation batch request requires one transaction ID plus optional others, and hot-path routing overloads are added only after realistic allocation profiling.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 keeps varargs packing rules and @SafeVarargs safeguards; avoid treating a benchmark from the Java 9 era as a portable allocation or speed guarantee.

notes.title: Use empty container results to make absence safe and consistent
notes.core: For a valid query yielding zero elements, return an empty collection or array rather than a null sentinel; callers can iterate and compose operations without a hidden null branch.
rules: Return an empty List, Set, Map or zero-length array for successful empty results instead of null.
Choose mutability explicitly: List.of() and Collections.emptyList() are immutable, while a fresh ArrayList supports mutation.
Avoid exposing internal mutable collections or arrays when snapshot semantics are required; copy defensively even on nonempty results.
For typed arrays, toArray(new T[0]) or toArray(T[]::new) give proper element types; profile any optimization claims.
Do not assume an empty collection is the same as an absent resource, failed lookup or denied operation—use distinct domain outcomes for those.
Maintain the documented empty-result contract consistently across pagination, filtered searches and optional query fields.
nuance: A shared empty immutable container can be reused safely; an empty mutable singleton would allow callers to corrupt each other.
The behavior of toArray(new T[0]) is useful in modern Java; pre-sizing is not a universal performance win or universal loss.
Java 21 Stream.toList() also returns an unmodifiable list; it is not interchangeable with every mutable collection result.
Collections.emptyList() allows a typed empty view without array allocation but does not imply a particular implementation.
For Optional<List<T>>, empty Optional can indicate no aggregate and present empty List can indicate an aggregate with zero elements—separate policy decisions.
notes.misconception: Returning null for no matches is a zero-cost optimization and consumers will reliably remember every null check.
notes.production_context: A merchant transaction search returns an immutable empty list for a valid filter with no rows while a missing merchant is a separate not-found outcome.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 List.of, List.copyOf, Collection.toArray(IntFunction), Stream.toList and records support clean empty-result contracts; do not use performance folklore as a correctness argument.
